statement: I can distinguish between someone I know and someone I have never met.
skill: Recognise familiar people and people they do not know, with adult support
activity: It's Good to Talk – Face to Face and Digital Communication

statement: I can recognise data online with adult support, e.g find images of myself and others on the school website/school social media page.
skill: Recognise that photographs of themselves or others may be seen online, with an adult
activity: Working Together – Awareness of Photos Online

statement: I can identify and use a range of media and digital devices from familiar experiences.
skill: Explore and use familiar digital devices for a purpose
activity: Let's Create – Being a Digital Creator
example: Use a tablet camera or digital drawing tool

statement: I can add my name to digital work.
skill: Begin to recognise their own digital work and that other work belongs to someone else
activity: Let's Create – Creating Marks On-Screen / Being a Digital Creator
example: Talk about whose picture it is

statement: I am beginning to become aware of the feelings of others.
skill: Express likes, dislikes and feelings and begin to consider others when using devices
activity: It's Good to Talk – Face to Face and Digital Communication

statement: I can sort and classify objects using one criterion.
skill: Collect, sort and match objects or pictures by one feature
activity: Data Data Everywhere – Sort, Order and Match
example: Sort natural objects by colour or shape

statement: I can recognise and follow instructions in the appropriate order to perform a task.
skill: Recognise, copy and continue a simple pattern or sequence
activity: Put On Your Thinking Cap – Sequences, Patterns and Instructions
example: Repeat a movement or bead pattern

statement: I can organise, select and use simple language to give instructions to others.
skill: Follow simple instructions in the correct order
activity: Put On Your Thinking Cap – Sequences, Patterns and Instructions

statement: I can organise, select and use simple language to give instructions to others.
skill: Give simple instructions to another child or adult
activity: Put On Your Thinking Cap – Sequences, Patterns and Instructions
example: Tell a partner how to move through a route

statement: I can organise, select and use simple language to give instructions to others.
skill: Explore controlling a programmable toy or on-screen turtle
activity: Show Me The Code – Explore Controllable Toys / Control On-Screen Turtle
example: Move a Bee-Bot along a floor mat

statement: I can talk about different forms of online communication, e.g. e-mail, messaging, video call.
skill: Talk about ways people communicate face to face and using digital devices
activity: It's Good to Talk – Face to Face and Digital Communication
example: Compare a conversation and a video call

statement: I can work with others to produce digital work.
skill: Work alongside others to make digital marks or pictures
activity: Let's Create – Creating Marks On Screen

statement: I can save and retrieve my digital work, e.g clicking icons, within apps, camera roll.
skill: With support, recognise how digital work can be saved and found again
activity: Let's Create – Being a Digital Creator
example: Reopen a saved picture with an adult

element: Sourcing, searching and planning digital content
skill: Explore familiar apps and tools for a purpose
activity: Data Data Everywhere – Supporting Role Play with Digital Applications
example: Use a digital till in a role-play shop

statement: I can create simple digital work.
skill: Make marks and pictures on screen using different colours or tools

statement: I can explore and use appropriate software to add text and images, exploring size and colour.
skill: Explore creating sounds or a simple musical sequence digitally
activity: Let's Create – Creating a Simple Musical Sequence or Soundscape
example: Create a soundscape for a story

statement: I can explore and use animation and video.
skill: Create a simple digital piece of work, supported as needed
activity: Let's Create – Being a Digital Creator
example: Record or illustrate a familiar story

statement: I can comment on work in relation to a single success criterion.
skill: Say what they like about their digital work or suggest one change
activity: Let's Create – Being a Digital Creator
example: Discuss a picture and change a colour
